description: Solo developer building an interactive digital storytelling flipbook exploring NASA's historic discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars for the 2026 Space Apps Challenge.
summary: "Ghosts of Exploration" is an interactive digital storytelling presentation and virtual museum exhibit exploring NASA's historic discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars. Developed as a solo project for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, this 7-slide visual narrative highlights iconic hardware left behind—such as the Apollo 11 Lunar Module descent stage, the Viking 1 lander, and the Opportunity rover. By treating these derelict structures as pristine archaeological time capsules rather than space junk, the project bridges space history with modern educational storytelling, inspiring the Artemis generation while fully utilizing public domain NASA data and archives.
details:
What it does & how it works:

This project is a curated 7-slide visual digital museum and storybook documenting abandoned NASA space hardware across the Moon and Mars. It systematically breaks down the engineering purpose, historical milestones, and legacy of iconic artifacts left behind during historic missions.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

It serves as an engaging educational tool designed for students and space enthusiasts (ages 8–14) to reframe historic space hardware as permanent archaeological monuments rather than waste. It fosters curiosity about space exploration and aerospace heritage.

Tools, Coding Languages, & Resources Used:

- Design & Format: PDF Presentation / Digital Storybook (Canva / professional document architecture)

- Data & References: Official NASA public domain repositories, including the National Space Science Data Center (NSSDC) Master Catalog, Mars Exploration Program archives, and NASA image libraries.

Creativity & Team Considerations:

Instead of traditional software code, this solo project leans into creative digital storytelling and historical curation. It solves the challenge by transforming complex space physics and mission logs into an accessible, beautifully structured visual narrative.
